title: Vision Claims Adjudication Guideline: Plan Payment for an Exam Visit
content:
**Vision Plans — plan payment for an exam visit**

**1. What an exam visit is.** An exam visit is the routine eye exam line of one claim of the enrollment, together with the claim's contact-lens fitting line when the claim carries no contact-lens line. A fitting on a claim with contact lenses belongs to the contact-lens order; spectacle lenses or a frame on the claim belong to the eyeglasses order.

**2. Which claim is decided.** The visit decided is the claim of the latest received routine eye exam line that carries no remark yet at a participating independent practice. When there is none, it is the same at a participating retail-chain location; participating means under a Cascade Vision Network Provider Agreement. When there is none of either, it is the claim of the latest received routine eye exam line that stands denied as not eligible at any location; an out-of-network visit already filed by the member and denied for eligibility is reprocessed the same way.

**3. Facts of the visit.** The visit's date of service, received date, network channel and provider agreement are those of its lines. The billed charge of each line is its retail charge. The patient's age is counted in whole years from the enrollee's date of birth to the date of service.

**4. Coverage on the date of service.** An exam visit is paid under the exam benefit only when the enrollment is active or terminated, and the date of service is on or after its coverage effective date and on or before its termination date when it has one. Otherwise its lines are denied as not eligible and nothing is paid.

**5. Exam frequency.** The routine eye exam line is paid only when the exam benefit is available again. The benefit is available again unless the latest routine eye exam of the enrollment whose remark is paid or out-of-network reimbursement paid blocks it:
- *Benefit-year basis:* a 12-month frequency is blocked by a latest exam in the same benefit period, and a 24-month frequency by one in the same or the preceding benefit period. A latest exam in a later benefit period blocks nothing. The benefit period is the twelve-month period starting each year on the enrollment's benefit-period reset day.
- *From-last-service basis:* the benefit is blocked when fewer than the stated number of whole calendar months separate the two dates, in either direction. A month is complete on the same day number.
- *Reversals:* when that latest exam is the only paid or reimbursed exam on its date and has been reversed, nothing blocks the benefit. Where there are several on that date, a reversal of one leaves the benefit blocked.

An exam line whose benefit is blocked is denied for frequency and nothing is paid for it. A contact-lens fitting line is not limited separately.

**6. Fees and copay.** Under the exam benefit the scheduled exam fee is **110.00**, every fitting line is scheduled at that same exam fee, and the exam copay is the plan's exam copay. The plan pays for each line the lesser of its billed charge and its scheduled fee, less the exam copay on the exam line. Out of network, the visit's fitting line, whatever its kind, is reimbursed at the lesser of its receipt and the plan's out-of-network exam amount.

**7. The payment.** The plan's payment for an exam visit is defined in this order:
1. The exam line's scheduled exam fee is multiplied once by the product of every fee ratio that applies. The lesser of the exam line's billed charge and that amount is taken, and the exam copay is subtracted, never below 0.00.
2. The fitting line's lesser of its billed charge and its scheduled fitting fee is added; an out-of-network fitting line takes its out-of-network amount instead.

The payment is booked on the visit's first paid line and rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Worked figure (hypothetical inputs).** A participating independent practice; the plan's exam copay is 10.00; exam billed 126.40; a contact-lens fitting billed 88.15 on the same claim, which carries no contact lenses; the exam benefit is available.
- Exam line: the lesser of 126.40 and 110.00 is 110.00, less 10.00, giving 100.00.
- Fitting line: the lesser of 88.15 and 110.00 is 88.15.
- The plan pays 188.15.

If the exam had been blocked for frequency, the exam line would be denied and the plan would pay 88.15 for the fitting.

**Frequency boundaries (hypothetical dates, from-last-service basis, 12 months).** With a last paid exam on 15 March, a visit on 14 March of the next year is 11 whole months later, so the exam is blocked. A visit on 15 March of the next year is 12 whole months later, so the exam is available.
